Set $5284 to $FF and $4D69 to zero. Set $4D6A to 7 only when $7F48 is zero and $7F47 is below $AB; otherwise set it to zero. Set $46 to $C0 and call $4655, $6D17, $6E12, $4A90, $18D8, $1863 and $7979.

Frame loop: updates countdowns, samples input, updates player and entities, renders display state and checks the selected player's meter before the next state dispatch.
Transfer control to the post-event tally entry at $0699. The game-exit flag at $042F–$0432 can branch here, and the status check at $044B can fall through here.

Dispatch through the little-endian pointer at $7F3F/$7F40. In the first-load entry capture it points to $0200; later load descriptors provide different targets, including $9661 in the second-load entry capture. The pointer’s runtime value determines the jump.
Converts the current grid indices and subcell offsets into four writable position bytes at $04a6–$04a9, used by entity initialization.

If bit $10 in the indexed state is clear, return with carry set. Otherwise prepare the revival-medicine message, clear bit $10 in the selected player's flags, and increment an indexed value until the selected value reaches $28; return with carry clear. The first increment uses X as left by the intervening calls.

Set shared sprite colours, hide the player and initialize eight display slots from position and frame tables. Wait for fire, mark 29 display slots free, wait for the fire input to change, then return to title for continue values $11 or $01. Otherwise save the display, load visual resources, show the continue message and select the left choice.
On each frame refresh the HUD and sample the controls. Test left first, right second and fire third; no selected input repeats the poll.
Place the two selection sprites using X=$E6 and Y=$E1, set the selection byte to $FF and resume polling.
Place the two selection sprites using X=$6E and Y=$E1, clear the selection byte and resume polling.
Fire with a nonzero selection returns to the title; a zero selection checks the remaining continue count.
If no continues remain, show the add-credits message. Otherwise spend one, restore the player meter to its limit, clear all three BCD score bytes and initialize the game display.
Display the message at $0678 and return to the continue-choice poll.
Three zero-terminated message fields followed by a $fe control byte. Text uses the captured character set.

Prepare the post-event tally: set the sound state, save the display, load the visual resource selected at $7F81, hide the player and clear the display-sort flag. Write $01 across 39 bytes at $D940; when the selected player meter equals its limit also write $01 across 39 bytes at $D990.
When the selected player meter equals its limit, pass $10 to the middle-byte BCD score addition routine. Otherwise skip this full-meter bonus.
Set the refill counter to the selected meter plus eight with eight-bit wrap, and set the score-conversion counter to that meter shifted right once.

On each conversion pass wait for frames, refresh the HUD, pass $02 to the meter-subtraction routine and $41 to the score routine. Decrement the conversion counter and repeat until it is zero. The first pass executes even if the counter began at zero.
Wait for a frame, pass $01 to the meter-addition routine, refresh the HUD and decrement the refill counter until zero. A zero initial counter takes 256 iterations because the decrement wraps.

Wait for fire. In two-player mode, when the selected player index is zero and the second player meter is nonzero, select the second player and initialize the game display. Otherwise continue at the stage-counter path.
Runs an alternate update loop with entity and completion scans. It patches an initializer call and preserves selected state in immediate operands before restoring it on exit.
Set the low byte of the following indirect-by-patching call from the indexed table.
Set the high byte of the patched call from the indexed table.
The call target is patched from the tables indexed by $7b before execution. The captured operand $ff00 is only the initial value; no bound on the index is established here.
Save the current value in the immediate operand used to restore it on exit.
Preserve the cleanup loop counter in the immediate operand reloaded after the calls.
Gates a down-input action on player and map state, chooses an action from a patched jump table and may initialize an entity. The selector's upper bound is not established locally.
When $6F equals 1, load the two immediates previously patched by $08E0 and restore them to $6F and $529C. Decrement $5243 modulo 256, then continue at $0853.
Immediate operand restored to $6F when $6F equals 1; another routine patches this byte before that restoration.
Immediate operand restored to $529C when $6F equals 1, after which $5243 is decremented. Otherwise this restoration is skipped.
Return if $72 is nonzero or $4DB3 is negative. A positive $4DB3 branches to $08AF; a zero value continues to the tile and position checks.
Require $527D to equal 15 and $7A to be nonzero; otherwise branch to $08AF. Compare $61D7 against six bytes at $7F77 through $7F7C, scanning from index 5 down to 0; if none matches, enter $08AF.

Return if $527C is at least 2. Otherwise store it at $4DAF and $4DB1, call $101F, set $4DB4 and $527D to 2 and call $0C2C. Clear $4DAF, $4DB1, $4DB0, $1178, $4DB5 and $4D55, set $4DB3 to $FF and return.
Return if $4DBB is nonzero; otherwise set it to $FF. Return if $5243 equals 2, or call $53E0 and return if carry is set; carry clear continues to the action dispatch at $08C5.
Patch the dispatch target low byte from the indexed table.
Patch the dispatch target high byte from the indexed table.
The four table entries resolve to the recorded destinations. The upstream selector has no locally proved bound; additional indices cannot be excluded here.
Copy $6F and $529C into the immediate operands at $0848 and $084C. Set $529C to $0F and $6F to 1, then return; a later pass through $0841 can restore the saved values.
The opcode at this branch is patched to BCC ($90) or BCS ($b0) according to the direction selected at $08f5. The captured BCC is not a fixed condition.

Call $190B and then $4454 without testing the carry returned by $190B. Clear $1AA0,X. When $7A is zero, copy $47/$48/$49 to $195D,X/$196E,X/$19A1,X, set $19B2,X to 1 and return. When $7A is nonzero, enter $09AC.
Copy $04A8/$04A9 to $194C,X/$193B,X and $04A6/$04A7 to $1990,X/$197F,X, then return. This path does not set $19B2,X.
Samples action state and updates horizontal movement, deceleration and vertical state. It uses active-low joystick values and recomputes the player grid position.
The captured item records and initialization produce indices 0–4; the consumer does not locally bound indexes supplied by other state.

Advance the alternating update counter at $1176. When its low bit is clear, reduce the player horizontal speed at $4DAF by one, clamping a negative result to zero; if speed was already zero, clear the direction at $4DB0. Continue at $0A2F to apply motion.

For the selected player, test flag $08, the fall-step value at $4DB5 and the sampled up input at $71. If the flag is set, the step is below 4 and up is pressed, decrement $4DE0. A nonzero result sets the fall step to 1; zero clears flag $08 and selects message 6, "Lost the Wing Boots." The counter advances on qualifying visits to this code, not on a verified video-frame schedule.

If $4DB3 is not 1, enter the input-edge check at $0B84. Otherwise, when $4DB7 is nonzero, select a sprite frame from $1177: add $72 when $4D55 is positive, or $70 when it is zero or negative. A zero result from the $72 addition also falls through to the $70 calculation.
If $1178 is zero, clear $4DB3 and $1178 and return. Otherwise write min($1178,8) to $4DB4, call $0D7F, decrement $1178 and return.

When $4DB7 is nonzero, $71 is zero, $76 is nonzero and $4DB5 is 2, clear $4DB8, set $1178 to 8, set $4DB3 and $4DB5 to 1, and set $4D55 to $FF. Use $4DBD to select a byte from $4DD5 and use it to index $0BC1 for $4DB4. Call $0D7F, then return to $0B41; otherwise jump to $0BC6.

If $4DB7 is zero, clear the animation index and delay and return. Otherwise, if both $73 and $74 are nonzero, set $4A to $1177 plus $66, clear the index and delay, and return. If either input byte is zero, enter the animation tick at $0BE4.

If $7A is zero, tail-jump to $0D56. Otherwise set $4DB6 to $FF and add $527D to $4DB4 modulo 256. A result below $10 skips the tile reads and enters $0C9D; otherwise check the next map row.
Use $6F3D+1 modulo 256 to select a pointer from $85CF/$8620, and use $6F3C as the column. Read the tile index and test bits 0 and 1 of $80CF indexed by it. If either bit is set, enter $0C81.
When $4DB3 is not $FF, repeat the attribute test for the next column. If neither low bit is set, enter $0C9D; otherwise enter $0C81. A $4DB3 value of $FF skips this second tile test.
Set $4DB4 to $0F minus $527D modulo 256. Clear $4DB3, $4DB6, $4D55, $4DB8 and $4DB9, then enter $0CA0 without calling $213E.
Call $213E for the entity-landing check, then continue at $0CA0.
Compare $49 with $A2. Equality enters $0CBD; a higher value enters $0CF6. For a lower value, add $4DB4 modulo 256: if the result is below $A3 store it at $49 and return; otherwise enter $0CB3.
Subtract $A2 from the candidate Y into $4DB4, set $49 to $A2 and continue at $0CBD.
Subtract $4DB4 from $4D69. If there is no borrow, store the result at $4D69 and tail-jump to $0D0A. Otherwise push the result and enter the map-boundary check at $0CCC.

Add 1 to $569E modulo 256, shift it right once and compare it with $7F4C. If below, call $2E77 and $0D0A, pop the saved difference, store its low three bits at $4D69 and tail-jump to $31A9. Otherwise enter $0CE8.
Pop and negate the saved difference modulo 256 into $4DB4, clear $4D69 and continue at $0CF6.
Add $4DB4 to $49 modulo 256. If the result is at least $E1, clear $4DB3 and replace the result with $E1. Store it at $49 and return.

If $4DB8 is zero or negative, update every eligible entry through $0D42. Otherwise use $4DB9 as Y, subtract 4 from each of $1A29,Y and $1A3A,Y, and store the resulting exclusion indexes at $0D54 and $0D55.
Scan X from $1B down to zero. Skip an entry at $27,X if it is $FF or X equals either exclusion index. Subtract $4DB4 modulo 256 from each remaining byte and return after the scan.
Scan X from $1B down to zero. Skip $27,X when it is $FF; otherwise subtract $4DB4 modulo 256 and store it back. Return after all 28 entries.

Add $4DB4 to $4D69 modulo 256. If the result is below 8, store it at $4D69 and tail-jump to $0DE9. Otherwise push the result and check $569D.

Set $1177 to $0E. Load the selected player profile from $4DD9 indexed by $4DBD; if it equals 3 and bit 0 of $5274 is set, return. Otherwise continue at $0E58.
Return if $E1 is zero. If $4DAF is nonzero and $4DB0 is negative, decrement $4DAF and return without changing direction. Otherwise enter $0E6A.

If the high byte at $48 is nonzero or the low byte at $47 is below $AA, enter $0F30. Otherwise subtract $4DB1 from $4D6A; store the difference and return if it does not borrow, or enter $0EED if it does.

Save the borrowed fine-scroll difference in the immediate operand at $0F07. If $569C is odd and (($569C >> 1) + 1) is at least $7F4B, enter $0F17. Otherwise call $2C8D, add 8 to the saved difference, call $0F63 and store the result at $4D6A, then call $3033.
Add 8 to the saved difference, XOR with 7, then add that value plus one to the two-byte player X at $47/$48. Clear $4D6A and return.
Add $4DB1 to the low byte of player X. If the result is below $AA, store it and its carry in the high byte; when that high byte is nonzero, clamp the low byte to at most $3A. Otherwise enter $0F4F.
Set the low player X byte to $AA, subtract $AA from the candidate position and patch that remainder into the operand at $0F5E. Subtract the patched remainder from $4D6A and return.

If $4DB8 is nonnegative, subtract the horizontal step from all 28 positions through $0F9F. If it is negative, derive two exclusion indexes from the contact entity slots and subtract through $0F7D. Only the all-position path applies a further low-byte subtraction after a high-byte borrow.
Scan X from $1B down to zero, skipping both exclusion indexes. Subtract $4DB1 from the low byte at $4C73,X and the borrow from the high byte at $4C53,X; store both and return after 28 positions.

Scan all 28 positions, subtracting $4DB1 from $4C73,X and the borrow from $4C53,X. If that high-byte subtraction borrows, subtract another 8 from the low byte modulo 256: SBC #7 executes with carry clear. The extra subtraction does not update the high byte.
Add $4DB1 to the 16-bit player X at $48:$47 modulo 65536. If the resulting high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $3A, replace the low byte with $3A. Return.
Set $1177 to zero. Load the selected player profile from $4DD9 indexed by $4DBD; if it equals 3 and bit 0 of $5274 is set, return. Otherwise continue at $0FF2.
